surfaces.part: front face with ticket windows and slots

answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a lighter salmon band (row 1 is a darker outline row, rows 2-4 are #f07864) that ends in a 1-row light front-edge line at row 5 (#fcc4a0). Below it the front face runs from rows 6-29 with windows and slots. The darker rows 6-8 under the edge line give a faint eave shadow, though the face has the same colour. This matches the 'cabinet: top 5 + edge + eave' reference. Silhouette is 14 wide with no side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, simple red vending-style cabinet. It has 10 visible tones per 16x16 tile, close to the hedge reference (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans dark red-brown against the red body rather than black. I count about 4 steps on the red body ramp (highlight, mid, dark, deep), plus separate tones for the panel, slots and buttons, against roughly 5-6 on the richer references. It reads slightly less rich than the stall and well, but it is not a flat sticker and holds up beside the hedge and bench. Because the prop is small and mechanical, its limited surface grain is acceptable.

answer.evidence: Rows 1-4 form a salmon band (#f07864) at the top. Row 5 is a distinct lighter 1-row front-edge line (#fcc4a0), and below it rows 6-8 are a darker red that works as eave shadow. The front face runs from row 6 to row 28 and holds the ticket windows, a slot and buttons. Row 0 and rows 29-30 are dark outline and base. The band looks like a top surface with an edge line, similar to the green cabinet reference (top 5 + edge + eave), not a plain front-facing strip. The eave shadow is only weakly distinct because it is the same color as the face below it. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a compact red vending cabinet with a lighter panel, a dark slot and small buttons. Its outline leans dark red-brown, and the 0% neutral dark-edge share confirms it is tinted, so there is no sticker look. There are no large flat fills (0% near-flat). It carries 10 visible tones per tile, which matches the simple hedge (9) but is well below the structured props that are the closest kind: stall-cheese (17) and well-roofed (20). It has only 14 colours in total, against 38-40 for those two. The red body ramp reads as about 4 steps, against 5-6 on the references, with little per-surface grain or per-element shading such as panel bevels, a worn edge or a shaded coin slot. It is clean and competent but a bit thinner and flatter than the stall or well, so it would look slightly under-rendered beside them.
